description: The brief's declared fields (audience, cuisine, creatorStyle, ...) render directly into the Task segment as short structured preferences, not as fenced untrusted text -- the same convention the add-ai-capability skill's own worked example uses for a declared template input. What still bounds an injected instruction hiding in one of them is the output channel: even an answer that behaves as if it 'obeyed' an injected instruction -- here, trying to add a field outside the declared concept schema -- is refused as an unknown field rather than stored. This is a structural containment proof about the output boundary, not a claim that a model declines the instruction; PromptEnvelope-kind fixtures cover the untrusted-fencing guarantee for capabilities that pass long-form creator or retrieved text through WithUntrustedText/WithSource instead.
